scope: Parts of the FEEDAP consumer-safety guidance that bear on what must be characterised: which material is tested, identity with the commercial product, identification of metabolites and residues, the purity exemption and the QPS exemption. Grounds the assistant only.

guidance.title: Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer
guidance.author: EFSA FEEDAP Panel
guidance.citation: EFSA FEEDAP Panel (Rychen G et al.), 2017. Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer. EFSA Journal 2017;15(10):5022, 17 pp.
guidance.license: CC BY-ND 4.0 (open access; redistributed unmodified with citation)
guidance.title_check_phrase: Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer
guidance.page_numbering: guidance_page is the PDF page number.

entries.title: What the consumer-safety guidance covers
entries.requirement: Guidance on assessing consumer safety of feed additives: studies needed (Section 2), requirements by additive (Section 3), highest safe intake and exposure (Section 4), MRLs (Section 5). Safety is assessed by comparing consumer exposure to residues with the safe intake.
entries.quote: The safety for the consumer is assessed by comparing the exposure of the consumer to residues in food products to this safe intake
guidance_anchors: The safety for the consumer is assessed by comparing the exposure of the consumer to residues in food products to this safe intake

entries.title: Test the active substance; the fermentation product must be identical to the commercial one
entries.requirement: Consumer-safety studies use the active substance. If it is in a fermentation product, test the fermentation product, which must be identical to the commercial one. With several active components, assess each and consider interactions; for complex mixtures that cannot be fully identified or separated, assess the whole mixture.
entries.quote: studies necessary to assess consumer safety should be carried out with the active substance [...] The fermentation product tested must be identical to that to be used in the commercial product [...] For complex mixtures, especially when the components cannot be fully identified/separated, the whole mixture should be assessed
guidance_anchors: studies necessary to assess consumer safety should be carried out with the active substance
The fermentation product tested must be identical to that to be used in the commercial product
For complex mixtures, especially when the components cannot be fully identified/separated, the whole mixture should be assessed

entries.title: Published studies: evidence that the additive is identical
entries.requirement: When data come from publications, show that the additive used is identical to the one under application, or that conclusions still carry over. For fermentation additives this includes the production strain.
entries.quote: evidence must be provided that the additive used in these studies is identical to that under application [...] For additives produced by fermentation, this includes the production strain
guidance_anchors: evidence must be provided that the additive used in these studies is identical to that under application
For additives produced by fermentation, this includes the production strain

entries.title: Justify omissions and deviations
entries.requirement: Applicants must justify omitted data and any deviation from the guidance.
entries.quote: Applicants should justify the omission from the dossier of any data or any deviations from the requirements detailed in this guidance
guidance_anchors: Applicants should justify the omission from the dossier of any data or any deviations from the requirements detailed in this guidance

entries.title: Aims of ADME and residue studies
entries.requirement: Establish metabolic fate in laboratory and target animals; identify and quantify toxicologically relevant residues (parent and metabolites) in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue; establish kinetics of total and marker residues.
entries.quote: to identify and quantify residues (parent compound and metabolites) of toxicological relevance in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue when required
guidance_anchors: to identify and quantify residues (parent compound and metabolites) of toxicological relevance in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue when required

entries.title: Radiolabelled test substance: justification and characterisation
entries.requirement: Justify the choice and molecular position of the label and describe its specific activity, radiochemical purity and stability.
entries.quote: A justification of the choice and the molecular position of the label should be given, its specific (radio)activity, (radio)chemical purity and stability described
guidance_anchors: A justification of the choice and the molecular position of the label should be given, its specific (radio)activity, (radio)chemical purity and stability described

entries.title: Metabolite identification threshold
entries.requirement: Identify all metabolites at >= 5% of the administered dose or >= 10% of total radioactivity in the animal (whichever detects more) and give a metabolic scheme. Identification means exact structural determination.
entries.quote: Efforts should be made to identify all metabolites present at 5% or greater of the administered dose or 10% of total radioactivity in the animal [...] Identification refers to the exact structural determination of components
guidance_anchors: Efforts should be made to identify all metabolites present at 5% or greater of the administered dose or 10% of total radioactivity in the animal
Identification refers to the exact structural determination of components

entries.title: Marker residue
entries.requirement: The marker residue is the residue chosen for assay whose concentration has a known relationship to total residues. Select it and give marker-to-total ratios for edible tissues and products. Consider non-extractable residues.
entries.quote: The marker residue is the residue selected for assay whose concentration is in a known relationship to total residues in tissues and products [...] Consideration should also be given to the amount and nature of non-extractable residues in edible tissues/products
guidance_anchors: The marker residue is the residue selected for assay whose concentration is in a known relationship to total residues in tissues and products
Consideration should also be given to the amount and nature of non-extractable residues in edible tissues/products

entries.title: Marker residue study design
entries.requirement: Minimum administration period 28 days (animals for fattening: the 28 days before slaughter); marker residue concentration measured with a validated analytical method of sufficient sensitivity.
entries.quote: The minimum administration period of the additive should be 28 days [...] Measurements of the marker residue concentration (MRC) should use a validated analytical method with sufficient sensitivity
guidance_anchors: The minimum administration period of the additive should be 28 days
Measurements of the marker residue concentration (MRC) should use a validated analytical method with sufficient sensitivity

entries.title: Relevance of residues
entries.requirement: First approach: total residues from labelled active substance are toxicologically relevant. Second step: discount the fraction incorporated into endogenous compounds and metabolites with reduced toxicological relevance. Structural alerts may help identify relevant metabolites.
entries.quote: total residues measured in edible tissues and products from target animals administered the (radio)labelled active substance are considered of toxicological relevance [...] Identification of toxicologically relevant metabolites can make use of structural alerts
guidance_anchors: total residues measured in edible tissues and products from target animals administered the (radio)labelled active substance are considered of toxicological relevance
Identification of toxicologically relevant metabolites can make use of structural alerts

entries.title: No consumer-safety studies: no exposure, not absorbed, QPS microorganisms
entries.requirement: No studies are needed if target animals are not exposed (with analytical data showing the substance is not detectable in feed at feeding), if the substance is not significantly absorbed (not for additives with a measurable nanoparticle fraction), or for QPS microorganisms and, in specified cases, enzymes and amino acids from them.
entries.quote: Appropriate analytical data to determine that the active substance (or related substances) is not detectable in feed at the time of feeding should be provided [...] except additives with a measurable fraction of nanoparticles [...] microorganisms considered by EFSA to qualify for the qualified presumption of safety (QPS) approach to safety assessment
guidance_anchors: Appropriate analytical data to determine that the active substance (or related substances) is not detectable in feed at the time of feeding should be provided
except additives with a measurable fraction of nanoparticles
microorganisms considered by EFSA to qualify for the qualified presumption of safety (QPS) approach to safety assessment

entries.title: Microorganisms and fermentation products: basic toxicity set
entries.requirement: Provide genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a 90-day oral toxicity study. For xenobiotic substances, the basic set augmented as appropriate.
entries.quote: For microorganisms and fermentation products, a basic set of toxicity studies should be provided consisting of genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a subchronic (90-day) oral toxicity study
guidance_anchors: For microorganisms and fermentation products, a basic set of toxicity studies should be provided consisting of genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a subchronic (90-day) oral toxicity study

entries.title: Toxicological studies not required for highly purified non-xenobiotic chemicals
entries.requirement: Toxicological studies are not required for highly purified non-xenobiotic chemicals, as a guide < 1% unidentified material on a dry matter basis. Characterisation of the unidentified fraction therefore decides whether this exemption applies.
entries.quote: non-xenobiotic chemicals highly purified (as a guide < 1% of unidentified material on a dry matter basis)
guidance_anchors: non-xenobiotic chemicals highly purified (as a guide < 1% of unidentified material on a dry matter basis)

entries.title: Safe dose: NOAEL or BMDL, lowest value
entries.requirement: The safe dose comes from the dose-response of toxicological or pharmacological effects, usually a NOAEL in mg/kg bw per day. Where only a LOAEL exists or dose spacing is wide, calculate a benchmark dose (BMDL5 continuous, BMDL10 quantal). Use the lowest NOAEL from all studies; justify any deviation.
entries.quote: The safe dose is derived from the dose response of toxicological or pharmacological effects and usually expressed as a NOAEL [...] In principle, the lowest NOAEL should be taken. Any deviation from this principle should be fully justified
guidance_anchors: The safe dose is derived from the dose response of toxicological or pharmacological effects and usually expressed as a NOAEL
In principle, the lowest NOAEL should be taken. Any deviation from this principle should be fully justified

entries.title: Highest safe intake: health-based guidance value
entries.requirement: The highest safe intake is a health-based guidance value (ADI, or UL for nutrients) = reference point (NOAEL, BMDL, LOAEL) / uncertainty factor. Default UF 100 (10x10) given genotoxicity, a chronic and reproduction studies; extra factor 2 if a subchronic NOAEL replaces a chronic one; UF <= 10 may be used with human data.
entries.quote: The health-based guidance value (mg of active substance per kg bw per day) is derived by dividing the selected reference point (e.g. NOAEL, BMDL, LOAEL) by an appropriate UF [...] The overall default UF of 100 (10x10 for inter- and intraspecies extrapolation) is normally used in calculating the ADI from laboratory animal data [...] If the NOAEL of a subchronic study has to be used in place of that of a chronic study, an additional UF of 2 should be applied
guidance_anchors: The health-based guidance value (mg of active substance per kg bw per day) is derived by dividing the selected reference point (e.g. NOAEL, BMDL, LOAEL) by an appropriate UF
The overall default UF of 100 (10x10 for inter- and intraspecies extrapolation) is normally used in calculating the ADI from laboratory animal data
If the NOAEL of a subchronic study has to be used in place of that of a chronic study, an additional UF of 2 should be applied

entries.title: Margin of safety when no health-based guidance value can be set
entries.requirement: For an additive that is not genotoxic, or is genotoxic and carcinogenic, and for which no health-based guidance value can be established, the margin of safety may be used: lowest NOAEL (usually from a 90-day study) divided by dietary exposure to the toxicologically relevant residue.
entries.quote: The MOS is calculated as the ratio between the lowest NOAEL usually from a 90-day subchronic toxicity study and the dietary exposure of consumers to the toxicologically relevant residue
guidance_anchors: The MOS is calculated as the ratio between the lowest NOAEL usually from a 90-day subchronic toxicity study and the dietary exposure of consumers to the toxicologically relevant residue

entries.title: An ADI applies only with a comparable residue pattern
entries.requirement: An ADI normally needs consumers to be exposed to residues comparable to those formed in the laboratory animal used to derive it; if metabolic proximity cannot be shown, test the target-species metabolites toxicologically.
entries.quote: If metabolic proximity between the laboratory animal used for deriving the ADI and the target species cannot be demonstrated, additional toxicological studies with the metabolites specific to the target species should be done
guidance_anchors: If metabolic proximity between the laboratory animal used for deriving the ADI and the target species cannot be demonstrated, additional toxicological studies with the metabolites specific to the target species should be done

entries.title: Consumption data and commodities
entries.requirement: Consumption comes from the EFSA Comprehensive European Food Consumption Database (latest survey per country and age class), converted to raw agricultural commodity equivalents. Age classes: infants <12 months, toddlers 12-<36 months, other children 36 months-<10 years, adolescents 10-<18, adults 18-<65, elderly 65-<75, very elderly >=75. Commodities: meat, fat, liver, other offals (including kidney), milk, eggs, honey, fish and seafood; mammals and poultry separately for meat, fat, liver and offals.
entries.quote: Consumption of edible tissues and products as derived from the EFSA Comprehensive European Food Consumption Database [...] Infants: < 12 months old [...] meat, fat, liver, other offals (including kidney), milk, eggs, honey, fish and seafood
guidance_anchors: Consumption of edible tissues and products as derived from the EFSA Comprehensive European Food Consumption Database
Infants: < 12 months old
meat, fat, liver, other offals (including kidney), milk, eggs, honey, fish and seafood

entries.title: Residue data used for exposure
entries.requirement: The dossier must allow estimating total relevant residues per commodity: arithmetic mean + 2 SD, or the highest single value with fewer than six animals. For multispecies use, the species with the highest residue per tissue represents poultry, mammals and fish. Meat is 80% muscle + 20% fat (mammals) or 90% muscle + 10% skin+fat (poultry).
entries.quote: the arithmetic mean plus two standard deviations or the highest single value in case of less than six animals [...] the value for the species with the highest concentration of residues in a given tissue of poultry, mammals and fish will be taken as representative [...] mammals 80% muscle and 20% fat, poultry 90% muscle and 10% fat (skin + fat)
guidance_anchors: the arithmetic mean plus two standard deviations or the highest single value in case of less than six animals
the value for the species with the highest concentration of residues in a given tissue of poultry, mammals and fish will be taken as representative
mammals 80% muscle and 20% fat, poultry 90% muscle and 10% fat (skin + fat)

entries.title: Percentiles and acute exposure
entries.requirement: Report the mean and the higher percentile (usually P95) of individual exposures per dietary survey and age class. Acute exposure is assessed for all available surveys, per commodity (RAC), on consuming days only.
entries.quote: the higher percentile (usually the 95th percentile) exposures based on the consuming days only will be calculated for each food commodity, dietary survey and age class separately [...] acute exposure will be assessed for all dietary surveys available and will be carried out for each RAC value separately
guidance_anchors: the higher percentile (usually the 95th percentile) exposures based on the consuming days only will be calculated for each food commodity, dietary survey and age class separately
acute exposure will be assessed for all dietary surveys available and will be carried out for each RAC value separately

entries.title: Chronic exposure: survey eligibility
entries.requirement: Chronic exposure assessments do not use dietary surveys with only one reporting day per individual, as these cannot assess repeated exposure. Per individual, total relevant residues are combined with average daily consumption of each commodity, summed and standardised by body weight.
entries.quote: dietary surveys with only one reporting day per individual will not be considered as they are not adequate to assess repeated exposure
guidance_anchors: dietary surveys with only one reporting day per individual will not be considered as they are not adequate to assess repeated exposure

entries.title: Outcome when exposure exceeds the safe level
entries.requirement: If consumer exposure at the highest proposed feed concentration exceeds the highest safe level, reduce exposure: lower the feed concentration and/or introduce a withdrawal period and MRLs.
entries.quote: If the highest proposed feed concentration of an additive would result in a consumer exposure exceeding the highest safe level, measures to reduce consumer exposure should be taken
guidance_anchors: If the highest proposed feed concentration of an additive would result in a consumer exposure exceeding the highest safe level, measures to reduce consumer exposure should be taken

entries.title: When MRLs and withdrawal periods are needed
entries.requirement: MRLs and a withdrawal period may be needed when residues could harm human health; generally no MRL without a withdrawal time; no MRL can be set without a health-based guidance value. An experimental withdrawal up to 12 h counts as practical zero-day withdrawal.
entries.quote: MRLs are generally not considered necessary if a withdrawal time is not required [...] In principle, the MRL cannot be set in the absence of such a value [...] An experimental withdrawal up to 12 h is considered a practical zero-day withdrawal
guidance_anchors: MRLs are generally not considered necessary if a withdrawal time is not required
In principle, the MRL cannot be set in the absence of such a value
An experimental withdrawal up to 12 h is considered a practical zero-day withdrawal

entries.title: MRL analytical method
entries.requirement: An analytical method of sufficient sensitivity must exist before an MRL can be set; its limit of quantification should be at least three times lower than the MRL.
entries.quote: The limit of quantification of the method should be at least three times lower than the MRL
guidance_anchors: The limit of quantification of the method should be at least three times lower than the MRL

entries.title: Calculating MRLs: variability
entries.requirement: MRLs are set per tissue/product from marker residue data; variability is normally reflected by the 95% confidence limit of the mean, or the highest individual value when it cannot be calculated. The process is iterative: choose the shortest withdrawal time with dietary intake of total residues below the health-based guidance value, derive MRLs, and lower them if the intake implied by the MRLs exceeds it.
entries.quote: Variability is normally reflected by using the 95% confidence limit of the mean
guidance_anchors: Variability is normally reflected by using the 95% confidence limit of the mean

entries.title: Extrapolating MRLs
entries.requirement: If feed levels are essentially similar, MRLs extrapolate within physiologically similar species (Table 1), to horses when MRLs exist for a major ruminant and pigs, and to other minor food-producing species except fish when identical MRLs were derived in cattle, pigs and chicken.
entries.quote: to horses when MRLs for a major ruminant and pigs exist [...] to all other minor species of food-producing animals except fish if identical MRLs were derived in tissues of cattle, pigs and chicken
guidance_anchors: to horses when MRLs for a major ruminant and pigs exist
to all other minor species of food-producing animals except fish if identical MRLs were derived in tissues of cattle, pigs and chicken
